newsitem.title: TURKMENISTAN: Turkmenistan opens $200 million gas plant tender.
newsitem.headline: Turkmenistan opens $200 million gas plant tender.

text.p: Turkmenistan's oil and gas industry ministry said on Monday it had opened a $200 million tender for the construction of a gas processing plant at the Saman-Depe gas field in the east of the Central Asian republic.

"In the tender -- a project costing around $200 million -- about 10 companies from Russia, Ukraine, Germany and France are taking part," an official from the ministry told Reuters. He declined to name the competing companies or give further detail sof the tender.
The official added only that preference would be given to those companies that would accept payment for the plant in natural gas delivered to the land-locked country's border.
The former Soviet republic's state gas concern, Turkmengaz, is organising the tender.

The mostly desert nation of four million sits on reserves of gas estimated at 21 trillion cubic metres. Gas output for 1997 is forecast at around 44 billion cubic metres (bcm), up from 35 bcm last year.

A new deal with Russia clinched earlier this year sees Turkmenistan aiming to double exports in 1997 to around 40 bcm, roughly half of which would go to Europe. The resource-rich country has been frustrated in its desire to increase natural gas exports by a lack of export routes.
